title: Thor: Strength and Protection
subtitle: A defender whose power is practical

learningObjectives.text: Trace the theft of Mjollnir and the condition Thrym sets for its return.
Explain how Þrymskviða uses disguise and comic reversal.

loss.author: Anonymous Old Norse poets
loss.locator: Þrymskviða, stanzas 1-7; local text normalized characters 264958-266219
loss.excerpt: 1. Wild was Vingthor | when he awoke, And when his mighty | hammer he missed; He shook his beard, | his hair was bristling, As the son of Jorth | about him sought. 2. Hear now the speech | that first he spake: “Harken, Loki, | and heed my words, Nowhere on earth | is it known to man, Nor in heaven above: | our hammer is stolen.” 3. To the dwelling fair | of Freyja went they, Hear now the speech | that first he spake: “Wilt thou, Freyja, | thy feather-dress lend me, That so my hammer | I may seek?” Freyja spake: 4. “Thine should it be | though of silver bright, And I would give it | though ’twere of gold.” Then Loki flew, | and the feather-dress whirred, Till he left behind him | the home of the gods, And reached at last | the realm of the giants. 5. Thrym sat on a mound, | the giants’ master, Leashes of gold | he laid for his dogs, And stroked and smoothed | the manes of his steeds. Thrym spake: 6. “How fare the gods, | how fare the elves? Why comst thou alone | to the giants’ land?” Loki spake: “Ill fare the gods, | ill fare the elves! Hast thou hidden | Hlorrithi’s hammer?” Thrym spake: 7. “I have hidden | Hlorrithi’s hammer, Eight miles down | deep in the earth; And back again | shall no man bring it If Freyja I win not | to be my wife.”
loss.note: Verbatim Henry Adams Bellows translation excerpt; whitespace normalized.

disguise.author: Anonymous Old Norse poets
disguise.locator: Þrymskviða, stanzas 16-20; local text normalized characters 267726-268388
disguise.excerpt: 16. Then Thor the mighty | his answer made: “Me would the gods | unmanly call If I let bind | the bridal veil.” 17. Then Loki spake, | the son of Laufey: “Be silent, Thor, | and speak not thus; Else will the giants | in Asgarth dwell If thy hammer is brought not | home to thee.” 18. Then bound they on Thor | the bridal veil, And next the mighty | Brisings’ necklace. 19. Keys around him | let they rattle, And down to his knees | hung woman’s dress; With gems full broad | upon his breast, And a pretty cap | to crown his head. 20. Then Loki spake, | the son of Laufey: “As thy maid-servant thither | I go with thee; We two shall haste | to the giants’ home.”
disguise.note: Verbatim Henry Adams Bellows translation excerpt; whitespace normalized.

return.author: Anonymous Old Norse poets
return.locator: Þrymskviða, stanzas 31-32; local text normalized characters 270240-270597
return.excerpt: 31. The heart in the breast | of Hlorrithi laughed When the hard-souled one | his hammer beheld; First Thrym, the king | of the giants, he killed, Then all the folk | of the giants he felled. 32. The giant’s sister | old he slew, She who had begged | the bridal fee; A stroke she got | in the shilling’s stead. And for many rings | the might of the hammer.
return.note: Verbatim Henry Adams Bellows translation excerpt; whitespace normalized.

narrativeBlocks.title: The hammer is missing
narrativeBlocks.body: Thor wakes and discovers Mjollnir is gone. Thrym admits that he has hidden it and names the price he wants for returning it.

narrativeBlocks.title: A disguise is proposed
narrativeBlocks.body: Thor objects to wearing a bridal veil. Loki argues that the giants may occupy Asgard if the hammer is not recovered; the gods then dress Thor for the journey.

narrativeBlocks.title: The return of Mjollnir
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translated; whitespace normalized): “31. narrativeBlocks.title: Read the poem's comic reversal
narrativeBlocks.body: Bellows translates the bridal disguise as comedy. Treat this tone as a feature of Þrymskviða, not as a rule for every Thor story.

quiz.prompt: What condition does Thrym set for returning Mjollnir?

choices.text: Thor must give up Mjollnir permanently

quiz.explanation: Thrym says no one will return the hammer unless he wins Freyja as his wife.
